item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00209","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C21","C05","C09"],"selected_candidate_label":"C21","confidence":0.86,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C21 plausibly supplied a material drafting template for the child’s treatment of a disputed Government ship-sale contract. Both documents explain the statutory pricing arrangement, identify a potentially inequitable contractual adjustment, direct or propose administrative examination of possible relief, and conclude that legislation should be considered if existing authority is inadequate. C05 supplies relevant merchant-marine and construction-subsidy concepts but not the child’s dispute-resolution machinery. C09 concerns congressional investigation of Maritime Commission ship sales but is only a narrow tax-return inspection order.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"the contract reflects certain errors in calculation, together with possible misconstructions of law, with the result that the operator may have been offered an excessive subsidy allowance","parent_excerpt":"The fundamental question presented by this bill is which of the two interpretations of the section 9(b) provisions results in the more equitable treatment to all parties concerned.","explanation":"Both frame a Government vessel-sale controversy as a pricing dispute involving legal interpretation and equitable treatment."},{"child_excerpt":"I recently requested that representatives of the United States Lines be invited to discuss with the Government possible adjustments in the contract.","parent_excerpt":"the owners who have taken the adjustments and now find that their contracts are disadvantageous should request the Secretary of Commerce to examine the possibility of relieving them from these commitments.","explanation":"Both use administrative reconsideration of existing ship-sale contractual commitments as the first corrective mechanism."},{"child_excerpt":"In the event you should find it impossible to take corrective action under existing law, please consider the kind of new legislation that could be recommended for this purpose.","parent_excerpt":"If it is determined that no authority exists to take such action, I believe the Congress should be requested to enact legislation which would permit these owners to be released from price adjustment commitments already made.","explanation":"This is a close parallel in both language and operative sequence: examine relief under existing authority, then pursue legislation if that authority is absent."}]}
